messages:
sam: Heads up — canary rollout is showing a noticeable tail in SSE streaming p99 (~+80ms) since last push. Noticed at ~15:12 UTC.

dev-bot: Deploy v3.7.4 -> canary group completed at 2026-03-17T15:12Z

aya: I see it on the dashboard. SSE p50 stable but p99 jumped. Tool-call-enabled routes look worst. KV cache hit rate for streaming sessions dropped from ~94% -> ~72% for affected traces.

john: I grabbed a flamegraph from a repro run. The stall happens during the tool-response path where we serialize tool metadata. There's an extra flush syscall introduced recently.

eli: PR #4128 touched the streaming protocol: added an explicit flush after every tool chunk to avoid partial frames in some clients. That matches the timeline.

sam: Can someone try to bisect to the offending commit? CI didn't alarm earlier, so maybe microbench coverage gap.

aya: Ran a local microbench with --sse-chunk-test. When tool headers are present median +55ms, reproduces reliably.

dev-bot: git-bisect started (good: v3.7.3, bad: v3.7.4)

john: Bisect landed on commit b6f3a2e (streamer/proto/handshake.go & runtime/kernel-routing tweak). The only notable change: WriteHeaderAndFlush() after each tool chunk. If I revert just that flush locally, the spike goes away.

eli: Reverting flush fixes latency but reintroduces partial-frame behavior for a handful of older tool clients we were trying to protect. So it's not a straight revert without further mitigation.

aya: Observed root cause chain: explicit flush -> many small write syscalls -> kernel chooses SMALL_RING socket path / different TCP coalescing -> runtime's kernel-routing ends up on a different kernel code path with higher per-call overhead. That interacts poorly with KV prefetch activity: the KV LRU lock gets hot and contributes another 10-20ms. Together they explain the p99 tail.

sam: TL;DR: protocol-level flush + kernel path selection + kv-lock contention = long tails on SSE tool flows.

john: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert explicit per-chunk flush in runtime (PR #4132-revert-proto-flush) and instead implement buffered writes with an end-of-chunk marker so we avoid syscall-per-tool-call. Code sketch:
```
// old
w.Write(header)
w.Flush()
// new
buf.Write(header)
if buf.Len() > 1024 || endOfChunk { flush }
```

eli: That sounds right. For clients that break on partial frames, we can add a negotiated handshake flag so only opted-in clients get the non-flush behavior.

aya: I've opened issue #762 to add a streaming microbench to CI that gates on sse p99 <= 200ms and to capture kernel-path histograms. Also added a dashboard panel and an alert for sudden kv-hit-rate drops on streaming routes.

devops: Rolling back canary now and holding rollout until we have the revert PR and CI test.

sam: Good. Action items: eli to open revert PR; john to add buffered writer patch and kernel-path telemetry; aya to add CI microbench + dashboard + alert; dev-sre to gather host-level socket histograms for the canary hosts.

dev-sre: Acknowledged — will collect tcp_sack/tcp_tw socket stats and ring-path histograms and post results in this thread.

sam: Thanks everyone. Once revert lands we'll re-run the canary with the new perf test enabled and monitor p99. Also let's avoid last-minute protocol flushes without a microbench next time. :thumbsup:
